_comment: klt erc supply spec for this repo's PLL layout -- the structural
power-delivery read that T1 item 11 (klayout-tools#2025, 2026-09-17) is
graded from. Issue #147.
Run it against the committed device-level layout record:
klt erc layout/pll/reports/20260906-195205-4a08c71/pll_top.gds \
layout/pll/erc-supply-spec.json --top pll_top --pdk sky130 \
--format json
`layout/pll/erc-reports/<record-id>/` holds the committed run. Read
`layout/pll/erc-reports/README.md` FIRST -- it states what this run does
and does not establish, and the repo's PLL layout is UNROUTED, which is
the dominant fact about every number in the report.
Layer/datatype provenance
Every layer/datatype below is resolved from TWO independent sources and
agrees in both -- never copied from another PDK's spec:
1. The sky130A PDK's own KLayout layer properties file,
`libs.tech/klayout/tech/sky130A.lyp` (volare-installed sky130A),
whose <properties>/<source> entries name each purpose:
poly.drawing 66/20, diff.drawing 65/20, licon1.drawing 66/44,
li1.drawing 67/20, li1.label 67/5, mcon.drawing 67/44,
met1.drawing 68/20, met1.label 68/5, via.drawing 68/44,
met2.drawing 69/20, met2.label 69/5, via2.drawing 69/44,
met3.drawing 70/20, met3.label 70/5.
2. klayout-tools' own curated sky130 deck layer table
(`src/klayout_tools/decks/sky130.py`), which states the identical
numbers and additionally documents the sky130 via-naming
convention this spec depends on: each via layer carries the LOWER
metal's own layer number (mcon at li1's 67/44, via at met1's
68/44, via2 at met2's 69/44), so `via`/68/44 is NOT met2.
stackup[] -- why each entry is here
- `poly` 66/20, role=gate. klt erc's own contract requires stackup[0]
to carry role "gate", so the stack starts at gate poly, not at a
metal. `active_layer` is set to `diff.drawing` 65/20 so the antenna
denominator is `poly n diff` (real gate-oxide area) rather than raw
poly area -- without it, every poly shape with no gate oxide under it
is treated as a gate and reports a non-physical antenna ratio
(klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md, "Gate area: poly n diff vs. raw poly
area"). This layout draws poly resistors (`poly.res` 66/13, the
loop-filter and PFD/CP xhigh resistors), which is exactly the
gate-oxide-free poly that fix exists to exclude.
- `li1` 67/20 -- sky130's local interconnect. Present in this stream
(650 shapes) and the level every standard-cell pin and every drawn
device pad actually lands on. `label_layer` 67/5 (`li1.label`) is one
of only two layers this stream puts net text on at all: the
sky130_fd_sc_hd cells label their SIGNAL pins there (A, Y, CLK, ...).
Declared so a gate net that is named at all reports a readable
`gates[].net` instead of null; no supply is labelled on 67/5 here.
- `met1` 68/20 -- present (130 shapes). `label_layer` 68/5
(`met1.label`) is where the standard cells put their POWER pin text:
29 `VPWR` + 29 `VGND` labels, one pair per placed cell. This is the
only layer in the whole stream carrying supply text, so it is the
layer the `nets[]` entries below are matched through, and omitting it
would make the supply check vacuous.
- `met2` 69/20 -- ZERO shapes in this stream today. Declared anyway for
one structural reason, not for completeness: met3 below does carry
geometry, and klt erc's connectivity model can only bridge met1 to
met3 through a declared met2 role (via 68/44 -> met2 -> via2 69/44).
Omitting met2 would silently make met3 an unreachable island. Its
`label_layer` 69/5 is declared on the same forward-looking basis as
the layer itself. A stackup entry naming a layer absent from the
given layout is explicitly not an error (docs/cli/erc.md).
- `met3` 70/20 -- present (3 shapes): the bottom plates of the loop
filter's three MiM capacitors (`capm` 89/44 carries their 3 top
plates). Real conductor geometry on a real supply-adjacent net, so it
belongs in the stack. `label_layer` 70/5 (`met3.label`) carries no
text in this stream; declared for symmetry with met1/met2 and so a
later routed revision that names a rail on met3 is picked up without
a spec change.
- met4 (71/20) and met5 (72/20) are deliberately NOT declared. They
carry zero geometry here, nothing in this block's routing plan or in
its MiM-cap stack reaches above met3, and declaring an unused top of
stack would add antenna levels that sky130's own antenna table does
not cover (docs/cli/erc.md: no met3+ limits are transcribed) without
adding any connectivity. Add them in the same commit as the first
geometry that needs them.
vias[] -- bridging the stackup roles
- `licon1` 66/44 (poly<->li1): 1173 shapes, the dominant contact layer.
- `mcon` 67/44 (li1<->met1): 706 shapes.
- `via` 68/44 (met1<->met2): zero shapes here -- this layout is
unrouted, so nothing climbs above met1 except the MiM plates.
- `via2` 69/44 (met2<->met3): zero shapes here, same reason.
The last two are declared so the stack is electrically continuous by
declaration rather than by accident, and so the identical spec still
reads correctly against the routed layout issue #18 is closing.
NOTE: `diff`/`tap` are not conductor roles in this model (diff is used
only as the antenna denominator above), so source/drain diffusion is
deliberately not part of the traced connectivity -- klt erc is a
wire/via connectivity model with no device recognition.
nets[] -- the declared supplies
- `VPWR` and `VGND`, both kind "supply". These are the ONLY supply
names that any geometry in this stream actually carries: the
sky130_fd_sc_hd standard cells' own power-pin text on met1.label
(68/5), 29 of each. Declaring both as "supply" is what makes a short
between them report as the severe `erc.supply_short` rather than the
general `erc.multiply_driven_net`.
- The top-level schematic (`design/top/netlist/top.spice`) names this
block's supplies `VDD` and `GND`, and the custom-drawn analog blocks
(pfd_cp, vco_ring5, loop_filter) are what those names belong to. They
are NOT declared here, and that is a deliberate choice rather than an
omission: no shape anywhere in this stream carries `VDD` or `GND`
text (verified by a full text dump of every layer -- the only strings
present are signal pins on 67/5, VPWR/VGND on 68/5, VPB on 64/5, VNB
on 64/59, and cell-name annotations on 83/44), so declaring them
would report `erc.unconnected_net` for "the label does not exist"
rather than for a connectivity defect, and -- worse -- once the
routed revision does label the rails, VDD and VPWR would resolve to
the SAME island and be reported as a false `erc.supply_short` between
two names for one net. The absence of analog-side supply labelling is
stated as a finding in erc-reports/README.md instead of being encoded
as a self-inflicted spec violation.
- `VPB` (nwell.label 64/5) and `VNB` (pwell.label 64/59) are body-bias
pins, not routed supplies, and their label layers are not stackup
conductor roles, so they are not declared. See the ties note below.
ties[] -- deliberately ABSENT (klayout-tools#2169)
There is deliberately NO `ties[]` section, and it is a recorded gap,
not an oversight. Declaring one on a real routed standard-cell layout
collapses the design into a single electrical island and reports a
FALSE `erc.supply_short` -- filed upstream as klayout-tools#2169 and
reproduced four ways in gf180-drone-fc's FRICTION F-034.
Because `ties[]` is omitted, `erc.missing_tie` is NOT COMPUTED by this
run (docs/cli/erc.md: "Omitted entirely -> erc.missing_tie is never
computed"). Its zero count in the committed report is an ABSENCE OF
EVIDENCE, not evidence of absence.
What stands in for it here: nothing that passes, and the honest state
is worse than 'unverified'. `tap.drawing` (65/44) has ZERO shapes in
this stream -- sky130_fd_sc_hd logic cells draw no taps of their own
(verified against the PDK's own sky130_fd_sc_hd.gds) and no tap cell
is placed in the divider row, so the well/substrate ties are not
merely uncomputed, they are demonstrably not drawn. There is no
`klt place-and-route` response in this repo and therefore no
`power.tapcell_master`; the only `klt lvs` run on record is the routing
spot-check's, and it reports `mismatch` (issue #18). See
erc-reports/README.md for the full statement.
